expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires the agent to actually read the bucket policy, identify the specific BucketAccessRule statement with an explicit Deny on s3:GetObject conditioned on aws:PrincipalArn (allowing only one specific role), confirm the reader role's identity policy allows the read, explicitly name the bucket policy (layer 4) as the root cause/DENIED_BY, and propose a concrete policy diff for human review.

The agent's actual response explicitly states it 'couldn't identify the denying policy' and that S3 calls were blocked, preventing it from reading the bucket policy at all. It only confirmed the role's identity policy is not the cause (partial match), but instead of finding and naming the actual bucket policy statement, it offers only speculative hypotheses (bucket policy deny, KMS issue, SCP/VPC endpoint issue) without confirming which one applies. It does not name 'layer 4 DENIED_BY' or provide a specific policy diff — instead it provides generic example commands to run and generic fix suggestions contingent on unknown results, explicitly asking the user to paste outputs back ('If you paste the bucket policy and the head-object output here, I'll point to the exact statement...').

This falls short of the expected output in multiple critical ways: it did not perform the root-cause read of the bucket policy, did not identify the specific Deny statement or PrincipalArn condition, did not name a definitive root cause layer, and did not produce an actual policy diff — only forward-looking suggestions contingent on further input. Additionally, the response partially violates the instruction to not say it will report later, since it invites the user to come back with more info rather than completing the full diagnosis itself.
